Fast boats from Koh Samui to Koh Tao take 1.5–2 hours, most stopping at Koh Phangan on the way, and cost about 700 THB. Slow ferries take 2.5–3.25 hours for 450–550 THB, and every public boat arrives at Mae Haad pier on Koh Tao. If you only want snorkelling and the Koh Nang Yuan viewpoint, our speedboat day trip (2,200 THB adult, plus a 250 THB cash island fee) is quicker and simpler than two ferry tickets.

Good to know: times below are from the Lomprayah timetable in force since 25 August 2026 and operator boards checked in October 2026; this page was last checked on 1 November 2026. Times change by season, so re-check at the pier or office the day before.

Is there a direct boat? Most boats stop at Thong Sala on Koh Phangan for 10–20 minutes. The 15:30 Lomlahkkhirin speedboat from Bangrak runs non-stop in about 1.5 hours, and Lomprayah's 08:00 catamaran from Pralarn also runs straight to Koh Nang Yuan, arriving about 09:45. "Change on Phangan" means you switch boats at Thong Sala, which adds time.

Koh Tao back to Samui

Return boats leave Mae Haad from about 07:00. Typical departures are around 07:00, 09:00, 09:30, 11:00, 12:00, 13:00, 15:00 and 15:30, with the last scheduled boats between about 15:00 and 16:30 depending on the day and operator. They land at Bangrak, Pralarn (Maenam) or Nathon. Fares are similar to the outbound trip (from about 600 THB). If you are staying on Samui and visiting Tao for the day by ferry, you get roughly 4–5 hours on the island. Buy your return ticket in the morning when you arrive, because the last boats fill up in high season and on days when earlier sailings were cancelled.

The day trip includes hotel pickup from most areas of Koh Samui (remote areas such as Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut add 400 THB per person return). The cancellation policy for day tours is a full refund 48 hours or more before departure, 50% at 24–48 hours and none under 24 hours; if we cancel for weather you choose a full refund or a new date.

How the day trip runs

  1. Morning Pickup from your hotel and transfer to the pier.
  2. Mid-morning Speedboat across the Gulf to Koh Tao.
  3. Late morning Snorkelling stops in Koh Tao's sheltered bays.
  4. Midday Koh Nang Yuan: lunch, the sandbar and the walk up to the viewpoint.
  5. Afternoon More snorkelling, then the run back to Samui.
  6. Late afternoon Transfer back to your hotel.

Exact times depend on the season and sea; your confirmation by email or WhatsApp after payment gives the pickup time.

Which Samui pier for Koh Tao?

  • Pralarn pier, Maenam: Lomprayah's 08:00 catamaran (the fastest morning option, with the Nang Yuan stop), the 11:00 slow ferry and the 14:30 speedboat. Best for hotels in Maenam, Bophut and Bang Por. Get directions
  • Lomprayah pier, Bangrak: the most departures, including the direct 15:30 speedboat. 10–15 minutes from Chaweng. Get directions
  • Seatran pier, Bangrak: Boonsiri catamarans at 08:00 and 12:30. Get directions
  • Petcherat Marina, Bangrak: Songserm speedboats. Get directions
  • Nathon: the cheapest slow ferry and the last boat of the day (16:00). Best for west-coast hotels. Get directions

For a day visit, the tour usually costs about the same as doing it yourself once taxis and the separate boat to Nang Yuan are added, and it removes the risk of missing the last boat back.

What to bring

  • Cash for the Nang Yuan fee (250 THB), drinks and tips; card machines are rare on Tao's beaches.
  • Reef-safe sun cream, a hat and a rash vest: there is little shade on the boat.
  • A refillable water bottle (plastic bottles are banned on Nang Yuan).
  • A dry bag for your phone and passport copy.
  • Seasickness tablets in October–December.
  • Shoes for the viewpoint climb.

Koh Nang Yuan rules

Koh Nang Yuan is a privately run trio of islets off Koh Tao's north-west tip, joined by a sandbar. It charges an entrance fee to protect the reef and limit rubbish.

  • Fee: 250 THB per adult, cash, paid on arrival. It is not included in tour prices. A reduced child fee applies. [check]
  • Plastic bottles: not allowed on the island. Bring a refillable bottle or buy drinks there.
  • Fins: banned in the Nang Yuan snorkelling area to protect the shallow coral. [check]
  • Drones: not permitted without permission. [check]
  • Viewpoint: a short, steep climb on steps and rocks; wear proper footwear, not flip-flops.

Arriving at Mae Haad

Mae Haad is Koh Tao's main village and only big public pier. Dive schools, cafés, ATMs and the ferry offices line the street behind it. Taxis on Koh Tao are pickup trucks with benches; prices are fixed per person by area, and the island's steep, rough roads make them expensive for short distances. Sairee Beach is about 10 minutes away; Chalok Baan Kao and the south-east bays are 15–25 minutes. Many dive schools collect their students at the pier. More on the island itself is on our Koh Tao from Samui guide.

Koh Tao at a glance

Koh Tao is small, about 21 km², roughly a tenth the size of Samui, and hilly, with one main west-coast strip and quieter bays in the south and east.

Roads to the east-coast bays are steep and partly unpaved. Renting a scooter on Tao is riskier than on Samui; many visitors take taxi boats or taxis instead. See our scooter rental guide for the licence and helmet rules, which apply on every island.

Sea and seasickness

The Samui–Tao crossing is about 60–70 km of open water, longer and more exposed than the hop to Phangan. From October to December, north-east swell makes it rough, and speedboats are sometimes cancelled. February to April is the calmest period; May to September is usually good. If you get seasick:

  • Choose a large catamaran over a small speedboat on choppy days.
  • Sit at the back, low down and in the open air, looking at the horizon.
  • Take seasickness tablets 30–60 minutes before boarding, as directed by a pharmacist.
  • Eat a light breakfast and avoid alcohol the night before.

Diving from Samui vs Koh Tao

Koh Tao is one of the world's busiest places to learn to dive, and courses there are cheaper than on Samui: a PADI Open Water course costs roughly 14,000 THB on Tao compared with around 18,000 THB started from Samui. If you have 3–4 days, staying on Tao for a course makes sense. If you want to dive from your Samui hotel, day trips run to Sail Rock (between Samui and Tao) and the dive sites around Koh Tao from about 4,650 THB. Dive season around Ang Thong runs about February to October, with the clearest water in March and April; Ang Thong is closed from 1 November to 15 December. See our Koh Samui diving guide, the Sail Rock and Koh Tao fun dives and Discover Scuba for beginners.

Combining Tao with Samui and Phangan

Koh Tao is the last island in the chain. Most visitors either visit for the day from Samui or stay 2–4 nights on Tao between Samui and Phangan. Our Koh Samui vs Koh Phangan vs Koh Tao comparison helps you split your nights, and islands near Koh Samui lists the closer options, from Koh Tan and Koh Madsum to the 42 islands of Ang Thong. If the sea is too rough for Tao, our Pig Island speedboat tour runs every day of the year from Samui's sheltered south coast.
